principles: Reuse the existing Lattice scope machinery instead of inventing a parallel gate.
Make scope facts structured and machine-consumed before improving prose.
Fail closed for unknown product, metadata, and fixture paths unless a registered classifier or explicit acknowledgement applies.
Keep exceptional repair visible as lower assurance, never as a silent pass.
drivers: Roadmap dependency order requires M1-M3 before later evidence/quorum/baseline milestones.
The story is high-risk because scope gates affect Lattice lifecycle correctness.
Parallel implementation needs disjoint file ownership and small reviewable surfaces.

options.name: A: Harden existing scope_contract and lifecycle classifiers in place
pros: Preserves current CLI commands and story lifecycle
Allows focused smokes to prove pass/fail/warn behavior
cons: Does not deliver the full M1-M12 roadmap in one story
Requires careful compatibility for existing ScopeCheckResult consumers

options.name: B: Build a new separate scope oracle subsystem
pros: Could model future roadmap concepts more comprehensively
Can start with a cleaner greenfield row schema
cons: Too broad for the dependency-safe wave-one story

options.name: C: Documentation-only wave with no runtime changes
cons: Does not satisfy the user request to begin development
Leaves known runtime gaps in row structure and acknowledgement audit context

chosen: A: Harden existing scope_contract and lifecycle classifiers in place
rationale: Option A implements the first dependency layer with the least duplication: it keeps existing commands as the product surface while adding structured rows, classifier reuse, audit context, and focused negative controls.

preMortem.scenario: Scope classifier becomes a broad directory exemption.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation treats .lattice, docs, or metadata directories as globally allowed instead of checking registered filenames and story ids.
preMortem.consequence: Unknown metadata or source drift can bypass scope gates and make later DONE evidence untrustworthy.
preMortem.mitigation: Centralize path classification and add negative smokes for unknown story metadata and ordinary undeclared source edits.

preMortem.scenario: Acknowledgement turns violations into silent pass.
preMortem.trigger: scope_contract_acknowledge hides out-of-scope paths from reviewers or changes enforce failures directly to pass.
preMortem.consequence: Exceptional scope movement becomes invisible normal behavior, weakening REVIEW and DONE gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep acknowledged paths as warn rows and add tests asserting acknowledged paths remain visible with repair/audit context.

preMortem.scenario: Stable row schema breaks existing consumers.
preMortem.trigger: ScopeCheckResult fields are renamed or renderers assume rows exist without preserving violations/warnings compatibility.
preMortem.consequence: Existing guard sessions, phase gates, and smokes fail or lose useful output.
preMortem.mitigation: Add rows as an additive field, keep existing violations/warnings/summary shape, and update tests around render output.

preMortem.scenario: Story expands into later roadmap milestones.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation starts changing host quorum, production authority, baselines, command center, or final certification because they are nearby in the roadmap.
preMortem.consequence: The branch becomes too broad for review and violates the scope anti-expansion goal.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the scope contract and PLAN file declarations limited to M1-M3 and document later milestones as non-goals.
